# inlaops - an introduction

This is a project that I wanted to have working for a while. 

Working in the life sciences sector I learned that [INLA](https://www.r-inla.org/) is a very popular package for modeling.

However, making it fit in the wider R ecosystem is a challenge. There are a few gaps, but in particular I was looking for a way to have a deployed model.

I thought that using it with `vetiver` should be the way to go, and so `inlaops` came into being. My specific case involves hosting on Posit Connect, but an API can be published in many ways, and this makes it suitable for different environments.

With `inlaops` one can follow the usual steps of fitting the model, and then making the model available on an API.

The Posit Connect use case is [documented](https://novica.github.io/inlaops/articles/connect.html) on the package's site.

`inlaops` was made possible first by being able to [install INLA](https://gist.github.com/novica/447c8f5c0a54386abdc113e618e58d66) from a local package manager, and then from `inlabru` having introduced [Tidy Postprocessing](https://inlabru-org.github.io/inlabru/reference/index.html#tidy-postprocessing). 

I expect there are some rough edges in the package. It works on my demo, but I would be interested in hearing feedback from users. 

The initial release is on its way to CRAN.
